evidence: The hunk shows `error(self, message: str, **fields: str | int | tuple[str, ...] | None)` restating the union already inside `Fields = dict[str, str | int | tuple[str, ...] | None]`; commit 43c641f extracts `FieldValue` and uses it in both places, exactly as proposed.
guidance_note: When a type alias wraps a value union, name the value union itself before a second signature needs it, so every reader annotates against one alias.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 43c641f only introduced the `FieldValue` alias, while the three-argument `self.raises(message, self, {...})` call that staled the docstring quote came from the original PR diff. The quote really did go stale, and shortening it to `self.raises(...)` keeps the docstring's real claim (an attribute call, not a bare name) without a second copy of the argument list.
guidance_note: When changing a call's signature, grep docstrings and test prose for quotations of the old call in the same commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the `f"{DEFAULTS_STANZA}.seed"` label feeding `settings=` predates 43c641f, which touched only model.py's alias. The reviewer was right that `init` published `[defaults].seed` where `add` published `seed`; 172e1fc changes it to `"seed"`, and the agent's own mutant caught that its first `assertIn` was a vacuous substring match.
guidance_note: When a display label is promoted into a machine-readable field, audit every call site's label against one vocabulary and pin each one with a line-exact assertion, not a substring `assertIn`.

evidence: Duplicate of F2, anchored at the test docstring. The stale quote comes from the original PR's change to `Reason.error`, not from 43c641f, so the flag is a false positive. The single edit to `self.raises(...)` resolves both threads.
guidance_note: When changing a call's signature, grep docstrings and test prose for quotations of the old call in the same commit.

evidence: The `port`, `seed`, `namespace` enumeration at model.py:194 predates 172e1fc, but the F3 fix was the sweep of the `settings` vocabulary: its reply quoted that comment as the contract and claimed the other labels were already bare identifiers, without noticing `add_cmd` also passes `"flags"`. 44a2d65 had already dropped the enumeration, and 86b9a59 added line-exact pins for all four labels.
guidance_note: When fixing one member of a documented vocabulary, enumerate every producer call site against the documented list before declaring the vocabulary consistent.

evidence: The missing `flags` value is real. The concrete repro is not: it claims `crom add ... --json` yields `error["fields"]["settings"] == ("flags",)`, but the agent notes `add` has no `--json`, which matches #33/F3's statement that `init` has none either. The agent pinned the rendered label line-exactly instead of adding `--json` coverage that cannot exist.
guidance_note: When fixing one member of a documented vocabulary, enumerate every producer call site against the documented list before declaring the vocabulary consistent.

evidence: `add_cmd` passes `"flags"` (cli.py:947), so the three-item list was incomplete. Rather than adding `flags` or calling the list illustrative, 44a2d65 removed the enumeration and kept only the claim the code cannot make (config-file key names, not display labels), which is sound. The fix-cause attribution is the same as F5.
guidance_note: When fixing one member of a documented vocabulary, enumerate every producer call site against the documented list before declaring the vocabulary consistent.

evidence: Fourth thread on the same model.py:194 enumeration. The defect (`flags` omitted) is real, and 44a2d65 resolves it by deleting the list instead of extending it.
guidance_note: When fixing one member of a documented vocabulary, enumerate every producer call site against the documented list before declaring the vocabulary consistent.

evidence: The hunk shows the original PR renaming `_errno_reason` to `_errno_detail`, and 172e1fc touches neither name, so the flag is a false positive. The test docstring at test_cli.py:2138 really still named the old function, and 44a2d65 updates it.
guidance_note: When renaming a function, grep the whole repo, test docstrings included, for the old name before pushing.

evidence: The AST-sweep test and its one-site docstring are original PR content (hunk @@ -2151 +2276), not 172e1fc, so the flag is a false positive. The agent confirmed four dynamic sites. In a3ca59a it replaced the hand count with an assertion that every unmatched `.error(...)` raise passes no keywords, which covers future sites as well.
guidance_note: When a docstring counts the exceptions a static check cannot see, assert the safety property over those exceptions instead of counting them.

narrative: The PR adds a per-Reason `fields` payload to crom's error envelope. Every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag except the `settings` vocabulary threads is a false positive on original-PR content: stale quotes, a rename, an undercounted docstring. The F3 fix normalized one label while treating an incomplete comment enumeration as the contract, which produced four duplicate threads about `flags` in round 2. Round 2 also carried the independent F9 and F10, so no round was purely avoidable.
guidance_observations: The agent mutation-tested its own new assertion and caught a vacuous substring `assertIn` before the reviewer did, then swept the same vacuity across four sibling tests.
The reviewer posted the same model.py:194 defect four times in one round, so the thread count overstates the review cost.
Several of the agent's fixes replaced stale enumerations with nothing, so the next label or site cannot make them drift again.

evidence: The new test repeats `any("--json" in option.opts for option in cli.main.get_command(None, name).params)`, the same predicate as the older test at ~2436. 2f1b70a extracts `_commands_offering_json()` and the agent reports `grep -c "in option.opts"` is 1.
guidance_note: Before writing a second test that introspects the same CLI property, extract the predicate the first test already uses into a shared helper.

narrative: This is a docs-plus-drift-guard PR with one finding: a duplicated introspection predicate. The agent extracted it and re-ran mutation checks on the README guards, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: After the extraction the agent re-mutated both README guards to confirm the refactor had not weakened them.

evidence: The `CromCommand` docstring claims `crom up --help` now works on a broken home, and the agent admits it had only measured that by hand. dc7f44a adds a test where bootstrap refuses, every command's `--help` must still answer, and `crom list` must exit 1 as the premise. The test was mutation-checked against readying moved into `parse_args`.
guidance_note: When a docstring claims a refactor fixes a user-visible failure, add a regression test that reproduces the failing environment in the same commit.

evidence: test_configwrite.py:291 still said `cli.main` calls `_bootstrap_user_config()` after readying moved to `CromCommand.invoke`. The agent found eleven such sites across five files and dropped the caller name from each while keeping the timing claim, rather than renaming to a new caller that could drift again.
guidance_note: When moving where a call happens, grep the repo for prose naming the old caller before pushing, not only the module being changed.

narrative: This PR moves readying into a `CromCommand.invoke` hook. Round 0 found a missing regression test and stale `main` attributions, which the round summary also listed outside the diff. Both were fixed in one commit, the second across all eleven sites, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The stale-caller sweep should have been part of the original refactor: the reviewer needed two places (an outside-diff note and an inline thread) to surface it.

evidence: The agent measured `Reservation(9224, "false", None)` rendering as pinned. It took the reviewer's validate-in-`_read` option and correctly rejected the `bool()` option because `bool("false") is True`. A mutant applying that coercion fails the new test.
guidance_note: When a diff gives a previously unconsumed parsed field its first consumer, add that field's type check at the parse boundary in the same diff.

narrative: This PR adds `crom doctor`'s port-ledger view. Its one finding is real: `pinned` and `source` were unvalidated and first published by this diff. The agent picked the correct remedy of the two offered and showed why the other was wrong.
guidance_observations: The reviewer's alternative remedy, `bool()` coercion, would have shipped a silent wrong value, and the agent encoded that rejection as a mutant-killing test.

evidence: No test reached `_leaks`'s `except OSError` arm. 5bdf5fc adds one using a regular file where the root belongs (`NotADirectoryError`), avoiding the reviewer's `chmod 0` (passes as root) and mock suggestions, and collapsing the arm to `return ()` fails it.
guidance_note: When a module's design separates 'could not check' from 'found nothing', write a test for each arm before review.

evidence: The original `_Gone` arm scanned only the default root, so a deleted config that had set `state_dir` reported clean. The agent kept the scan and added an `Unscanned` caveat rather than going caveat-only, which preserves the common-case finding. But 5bdf5fc also added an unreachable `_Fileless` variant that was deleted again in 00c6d93, and the both-rows arm later produced F3, F4 and F10.
guidance_note: Before adding a union variant for a state, confirm some input can reach it; here `_bootstrap_user_config` always writes the user config first.

evidence: 5bdf5fc made `_Gone` emit an `Unscanned` caveat, but the README still said a gone config 'is not one of those cases' and 'answers for real'. 66cfb66 rewrote the paragraph with a two-way split, because the third case the reviewer listed (`_Fileless`) had been deleted as unreachable.
guidance_note: When a fix changes behaviour the README documents, grep the README for the old claim and update it in the same commit.

evidence: Duplicate of F3: the round 2 review ran against 00c6d93 seconds before 66cfb66 landed the README fix, and the agent quotes the corrected paragraph.
guidance_note: When a fix changes behaviour the README documents, grep the README for the old claim and update it in the same commit.

evidence: `namespaces = {**registry.namespaces(), ...}` is original PR code that 00c6d93 did not change, so the flag is a false positive. The agent reproduced `staging: []` with the leak still on disk after `forget_mapping`. It drove the scan from the ledger via a new total `namespace_of` instead of the partial `parse_ref`, but its claim that a bad key yields only 'a namespace with no directory on disk' was false and became F11.
guidance_note: When a command enumerates entities, drive it from the register that cannot lose them (the ledger), not from an index whose own docstring says it drops entries.

evidence: The unguarded `entry.is_dir()` filter sits outside the `try` in the original `_leaks`, and 00c6d93 did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive. The agent reproduced PermissionError on Python 3.12 (`sub RAISED PermissionError`) against False on 3.14, and b908ffe moves the filter under the one handler.
guidance_note: When wrapping a filesystem read in an OSError handler, include every stat-ing call on its results, and run the test suite on the minimum supported interpreter.

evidence: The original `_leaks` docstring says `seed._staged` is the only dot-prefixed writer, but `migrate._move_staged` writes `.<name>.partial` into the same user root, and that file can hold the only copy of the profile. b908ffe takes the exclusion remedy through a shared `migrate.STAGING_SUFFIX`, with a test that also asserts the real leak is still found.
guidance_note: Before writing 'X is the only writer of Y' in a docstring that justifies a heuristic, grep for every code path that creates paths matching Y.

evidence: The README's 'a symlink counts as the link' sentence is in the original PR text (visible in F3's hunk), and b908ffe's README change did not touch it, so the flag is a false positive. `measure` adds only `S_ISREG` entries, and the agent measured a 65-byte link contributing 0.
guidance_note: When documenting what a size counts, state it from the measuring function's actual predicate (`S_ISREG` under `lstat`) rather than from intent.

evidence: The 'left behind by an interrupted seed' summary line is original PR code (hunk @@ -1615), contradicting `doctor.Staged`'s own caveat that a running seed looks identical. b908ffe only quoted that line in a docstring, so the flag is a false positive. 469dc27 aligns `--help` and the summary line to the careful claim.
guidance_note: When a domain type's docstring carries a safety caveat, carry it into the CLI help and summary text the user actually reads.

evidence: F2's fix (5bdf5fc) made the `_Gone` arm append an `Unscanned` after `*_leaks(...)`, which can itself return an `Unscanned`. A broken root then yields two rows, and the agent reproduced the summary claiming '2 namespace(s)' for one namespace. The agent kept both true rows, counted distinct namespaces, and documented the duplicate-namespace shape for `--json` consumers.
guidance_note: When an arm starts emitting more than one row per key, re-check every consumer that counts or keys by that key in the same commit.

evidence: `namespace_of`, added in b908ffe as F5's fix, returns `ref.split("/", 1)[0]` unvalidated. The agent reproduced a decoy in the shared root reported as a leak, and `../dev` escaping the root, so the reviewer understated it. 469dc27 returns `str | None` gated on `_NAME_RE` instead of the reviewer's `or "<unknown>"` patch, which would have left `..` traversing.
guidance_note: When a fix turns untrusted text into a path component, validate it with the same name grammar the writers enforce before the first `/` join, and test with `..` and empty segments.

narrative: This PR adds `crom doctor`'s staging-leak survey and ran to the five-review-round cap. Two fixes cost later rounds. F2's both-halves `_Gone` arm left the README stale (F3, F4) and could double-count unscanned namespaces (F10). F5's ledger-driven scan introduced an unvalidated `namespace_of` that let a bad key scan the shared root or escape it (F11). Round 1 existed only for F2's README drift. The other later findings (F6, F7, F8, F9) were pre-existing defects in original code, and the POST-REVIEW/NAMED-FIX flags on them are false positives.
guidance_observations: The F2 fix added a `_Fileless` variant that the next commit deleted as unreachable: one round of design churn that checking reachability first would have saved.

Fix replies made confident safety claims ('the worst a hand-edited key can produce is a namespace with no directory') that the next round disproved; such claims deserve a hostile-input test before they are posted.
The agent consistently reproduced findings and mutation-checked its new tests, which is why its different-fix choices held up.
